So, we need to find the rank of the matrix $T.$ We reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 6 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $T$ has $1$ pivot column, we have that 

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=1.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186123296 :answer-field/correct 17592186123301 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id 17592186124519 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-59614e83-6cc0-5ed3-9c08-72ebbf1a6792" "question-a744da17-c832-5e19-8de7-48116074536b" "question-dca0d5db-2f8d-5d5d-b6ae-e11ba42097a0"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-59614e83-6cc0-5ed3-9c08-72ebbf1a6792" :question/id #uuid "59614e83-6cc0-5ed3-9c08-72ebbf1a6792" :question/math-academy-id "q-38011" :question/problem "The linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{4}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{4}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{4},$ where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{4} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}+4{x}_{4} \\ 7{x}_{4}-4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & 5 & -2 & 4 \\ -4 & -1 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b]$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & -2 & 4 & 5 \\ -4 & -1 & -3 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 10 & -10 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -1 & 17 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-\frac{3}{2}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 10 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -16 & 32 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has three pivot columns (the $1$st, $2$nd and the $4$th). Hence ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. 
Now, from the third equation we get 

$$
-16{x}_{4}=32\,⟹\,{x}_{4}=-2.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation gives

$$
2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}+10(-2)=-10\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=5+{x}_{3}.
$$

Then, substituting ${x}_{2}=5+{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}=2$ into the first equation we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}+(5+{x}_{3})-2(-2)=5\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-4-{x}_{3}.
$$

As a result, the general solution is given by 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4-{x}_{3} \\ 5+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=0$, we have

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

where $T(x)=b.$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{4}=-4+5-2=-1.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d7a56c57-7ab7-579a-a5d2-335e803bfe6b"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-d7a56c57-7ab7-579a-a5d2-335e803bfe6b" :answer-field/id #uuid "d7a56c57-7ab7-579a-a5d2-335e803bfe6b" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-162ce159-8146-5343-b673-2bb04870d49d" :answer-field/choices ["answer-162ce159-8146-5343-b673-2bb04870d49d" "answer-3b8760df-a057-50f7-9fb8-ea0e266e838b" "answer-33a2a109-2527-55af-bbae-ca17356c27f6" "answer-d52e325b-57b3-5106-9fdd-f84a1cb74aaa" "answer-d6c73eea-57b4-5135-a689-e2351a61cbfd"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-162ce159-8146-5343-b673-2bb04870d49d" :answer/id #uuid "162ce159-8146-5343-b673-2bb04870d49d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3b8760df-a057-50f7-9fb8-ea0e266e838b" :answer/id #uuid "3b8760df-a057-50f7-9fb8-ea0e266e838b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-7" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-33a2a109-2527-55af-bbae-ca17356c27f6" :answer/id #uuid "33a2a109-2527-55af-bbae-ca17356c27f6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d52e325b-57b3-5106-9fdd-f84a1cb74aaa" :answer/id #uuid "d52e325b-57b3-5106-9fdd-f84a1cb74aaa" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d6c73eea-57b4-5135-a689-e2351a61cbfd" :answer/id #uuid "d6c73eea-57b4-5135-a689-e2351a61cbfd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "b\notin \text{Im}(T)" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-a744da17-c832-5e19-8de7-48116074536b" :question/id #uuid "a744da17-c832-5e19-8de7-48116074536b" :question/math-academy-id "q-38618" :question/problem "The linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{4}$ are given below. $$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & 1 & -6 & -5 \\ 3 & 5 & -16 & 10 & 4 \\ -1 & -1 & 5 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -10 & 1 & -8 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-4{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 & -20 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 & -5 & -2 \\ 3 & 7 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 7 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{2}{7}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 7 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Hence, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable.
Now, from the second equation, we get 

$$
7{x}_{2}-7{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{2}={x}_{3}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}+3({x}_{3})-2{x}_{3}=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2-{x}_{3}.
$$

As a result, the general solution is given by 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=1$, we have

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $T(x)=b.$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1+1=2.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-1e5a8161-1b5e-5e2b-bdbc-8100f0ce6ace"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]}
